Fu-En Yang

Research Scientist · NVIDIA Research

I am a Research Scientist at NVIDIA Research, developing generalizable and agentic systems for robot learning and control. My work connects world–action modeling, embodied reasoning, and action to help robots understand physical dynamics, anticipate the consequences of their decisions, and adapt their behavior across tasks and environments.

I received my Ph.D. from National Taiwan University in July 2023, advised by Prof. Yu-Chiang Frank Wang. Previously, I was a research intern at NVIDIA Research (Feb.–Aug. 2023) and a Ph.D. program researcher at ASUS AICS (Sep. 2020–Oct. 2022), working on model personalization, vision-language models, and visual transfer learning.

I received my bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering from National Taiwan University in 2018.

EmailCVGoogle ScholarLinkedInX / TwitterGitHub

Research Interests

My research focuses on generalizable and agentic robot intelligence. I study world modeling and world–action modeling to understand physical dynamics, predict action outcomes, and reason through imagined futures. By connecting these predictive models with agentic robotics, I aim to build robots that plan over long horizons, learn from interaction, and adapt to unfamiliar tasks and environments.
